100.name: Savanna Portage State Park
100.description: This state park, Minnesota’s third largest, has nearly 16,000 acres to explore. Swim or fish in Loon Lake, hike the Continental Divide Trail, or go mountain biking, snowmobiling, or skiing.

101.name: Schoolcraft State Park
101.description: This park is named for Henry Rowe Schoolcraft, who charted the headwaters of the Mississippi River with Anishinabe guide Ozawindib. Quiet trails lead through a virgin pine forest.

102.name: Lake Vermilion-Soudan Underground Mine State Park
102.description: Journey a half-mile underground to explore the world of mining or tour a fascinating physics lab. This park preserves five miles of shoreline and public access to a 40,000-acre lake with 368 islands. Hike the 2.4-mile Alaska Shaft trail for an overview.

1137.name: Pyrite Campground - Off Highway Vehicle Rec Area

103.name: Temperance River State Park
103.description: Waterfalls, deep potholes, and eye-catching geologic features are everywhere along the deep, narrow Temperance River gorge. Take the Superior Hiking Trail through the gorge to Carlton Peak (el. 1,526 ft.) or fish one of the park’s designated trout streams.

104.name: Tettegouche State Park
104.description: A spectacular example of the North Shore’s natural beauty, this park has scenic overlooks galore. Hikers and skiers can view the Sawtooth Mountains and several waterfalls along the Baptism River, including High Falls, the highest waterfall entirely inside Minnesota’s border.

105.name: Whitewater State Park
105.description: This park is also an angler’s paradise, with brown, brook, and rainbow trout swimming in the spring-fed Whitewater River and Trout Run Creek. Other attractions include the swimming beach, year-round naturalist programs, and a noticeable absence of mosquitoes.

106.name: Wild River State Park
106.description: This park has extensive trails for hiking, horseback riding, and skiing. Have fun camping and canoeing on the St. Croix River during warmer months. Naturalist programs are offered year-round.

107.name: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park
107.description: Highlights of this park include year-round nature and history programs, self-guided interpretive trails and a 100-foot fire tower that you can climb for a majestic view of Mille Lacs Lake.

108.name: Banning State Park
108.description: Explore the Quarry Loop Trail, which winds through the quiet ruins of overgrown quarry buildings and sandstone rock formations, and don’t miss beautiful Wolf Creek Falls.

109.name: Beaver Creek Valley State Park
109.description: Home to a great variety of wildflowers and birds, this bluffland park also boasts one of the best trout streams in southeastern Minnesota.

110.name: Big Bog State Recreation Area
110.description: A mile-long boardwalk leads through a bog at this recreation area in northern Minnesota, which offers incredible birdwatching, with more than 300 species of birds.   The sandy swimming beach on Upper Red Lake is ideal for children.

111.name: Big Stone Lake State Park
111.description: The source of the Minnesota River, this 30-mile-long lake on the South Dakota-Minnesota border is known for great walleye fishing.

112.name: Buffalo River State Park
112.description: Explore one of Minnesota's largest remnant prairies on foot or skis. In addition to 250 species of wildflowers and grasses, the park has an abundance of colorful butterflies and birds.

113.name: Carley State Park
113.description: Towering white pines share this bluffland landscape with oak forests and delicate wildflowers, including beautiful bluebells in May. Catch brown trout in the Whitewater River.

114.name: Crow Wing State Park
114.description: Located at the confluence of the Crow Wing and Mississippi rivers, this park is a nature lover’s delight. Hike the famous Woods Trail and check out the view from Chippewa Lookout.

115.name: Flandrau State Park
115.description:
With a beach, a play structure, volleyball, cornhole, and a large enclosed picnic shelter, Flandrau State Park – adjacent to the city of New Ulm – has several facilities for family reunions and other gatherings.
Due to a campground improvement project within our rustic campground - some sites have been renumbered. Please look at the map when choosing your site, sites you may have reserved in the past may have new numbers.
*** Swim Pond Season Dates: First Friday of June through the Third Sunday of August ***

116.name: Fort Ridgely State Park
116.description: This park features a historic fort and horse trails, and has a good sliding hill in the winter. A bike trail connects the park to the town of Fairfax.

118.name: Gooseberry Falls State Park
118.description: This park is the gateway to the North Shore, known for its spectacular waterfalls and Northwoods wildlife. Bring bikes and ride the Gitchi-Gami State Trail to Split Rock Lighthouse State Park.

119.name: Hayes Lake State Park
119.description: Some days it’s just you, loons, and moose, while you traverse around Hayes Lake. Enjoy fishing, swimming, and canoeing in the lake. Park trails connect with Beltrami Island State Forest.

122.name: Judge C. R. Magney State Park
122.description: Enjoy trout fishing and spectacular scenery as you hike along the Brule River to the famous Devil’s Kettle waterfall, where half of the river plunges 50 feet into a pool, and the rest disappears.

123.name: Lac qui Parle State Park
123.description: Visit the “lake that speaks” in spring or fall to see and hear thousands of geese and other migratory waterfowl. While in the area, visit the 27,000-acre Lac qui Parle Wildlife Management Area.

124.name: Lake Bemidji State Park
124.description: Explore this park’s tamarack bog in spring or summer to see some of Minnesota’s carnivorous plants. Swim, fish, and boat in the summer or ski and snowshoe in the winter. Naturalist-led activities take place year-round.

125.name: Lake Bronson State Park
125.description:
Expect big things when you visit this park. It has one of the largest observation towers of any Minnesota state park, and an extensive trail system for hiking, biking, skiing, and snowmobiling.

The Two Rivers Campground is not accessible to large RV’s or campers.  The road to the campground is narrow and winding.  All roads in the campground loops are very narrow and will not allow large units to maneuver through.

842.name: Two Rivers Campground Not accessible to large RV's

126.name: Lake Carlos State Park
126.description: Water recreation of all kinds makes this park a popular summer vacation destination. Clear and deep, Lake Carlos is an ideal setting for swimming, fishing, and boating fun.

127.name: Maplewood State Park
127.description: Swim, fish, paddle, and picnic surrounded by rolling, forested hills here at Maplewood State Park, a name synonymous with stunning fall color.  An extensive network of multi-purpose trails winds around eight major lakes and many ponds.

128.name: Split Rock Creek State Park
128.description:
Located 3.5 hours SW of Minneapolis - Not on Lake Superior
Swim, fish, or boat the waters of Split Rock Lake, the largest body of water in the county. Stop by the Beach Side Trail Center to discover more about the area, and be sure to visit the nearby Pipestone National Monument.

129.name: Minnesota Valley State Recreation Area
129.description: Just minutes from the Twin Cities, this state recreation area provides access to miles of trails, including the multi-use Minnesota Valley State Trail that parallels the Minnesota River.

130.name: Father Hennepin State Park
130.description: Among the wildlife inhabiting the hardwood forest at this park are several white deer. Bike the Soo Line trail, which runs by the park, then enjoy swimming and fishing in beautiful Mille Lacs Lake.

131.name: Minneopa State Park
131.description: The word “minneopa” comes from the Dakota language and is interpreted to mean “water falling twice,” referring to the park’s two beautiful waterfalls. A short walk leads to an overlook.

132.name: Camden State Park
132.description: Swim, picnic, and fish surrounded by spring wildflowers or fall color.  Brawner Lake has an abundance of bass and bluegill, and the Redwood River is stocked with brown trout.

133.name: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park
133.description: Spring wildflowers and fall color abound at this park, where Hidden Falls, the rare dwarf trout lily, and one of the last extensive stands of maple-basswood forest can be found.

134.name: Myre-Big Island State Park
134.description: Birds and biking are the big attractions at this park. Albert Lea Lake and surrounding marshes draw hundreds of waterfowl during migration. The six-mile Blazing Star State Trail is paved and connects the park to Albert Lea.

135.name: Zippel Bay State Park
135.description: Way up north on Lake of the Woods, enjoy swimming and beachcombing along miles of white sand in the company of white pelicans, double-crested cormorants, and piping plovers. Canoe in the protected Zippel Bay or head out onto Lake of the Woods for world-class walleye fishing. In winter, ski or snowshoe through quiet jack pine and birch forests.

136.name: Bear Head Lake State Park
136.description: Voted America’s Favorite Park in 2010, it offers excellent canoeing, fishing, and camping in a Northwoods setting similar to the nearby Boundary Waters Canoe Area.

809.name: Group Camp - tents only, no campers/RV's allowed

137.name: La Salle Lake State Recreation Area
137.description: Open since 2011 and currently under development, Minnesota's newest state recreation area offers a great wilderness experience and peaceful getaway amid red and jack pine forests and woodlands. A fish haven, La Salle Lake is the deepest natural inland lake in the state. Other highlights include a coldwater stream, a scientific and natural area, and a pristine stretch of the Mississippi River.

217.name: Sand Dunes State Forest
217.description:
Bob Dunn offers two large group sites. There is a pump for water, fire rings, and picnic tables. Only Horse Camp Site 1 has a picnic shelter. Vault toilets are in the campground 

Ann Lake offers four group sites! Pine View 1, Pine View 2, and Pine View 3, all have vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables. These are only hike in sites! Pine View has a water spigot there in the main lot for all three sites. Lake View is a large site for tents and is also hike in only. There are two vault toilets as well. There is a solar well at the site for water. There is a beautiful view of Ann Lake and

66.name: Blue Mounds State Park
66.description: Rock climbing and birdwatching are popular activities at Blue Mounds, where Sioux quartzite cliffs rise high above the surrounding tall-grass prairie that is home to buffalo.

67.name: St. Croix State Park
67.description: There are two scenic rivers to fish and paddle here at Minnesota’s largest state park, plus an extensive trail system, a swimming beach, a fire tower, and seasonal naturalist programs

1081.name: Head of the Rapids Group Center

68.name: Cascade River State Park
68.description: Wildlife and waterfalls will thrill visitors to this scenic spot in the Sawtooth Mountains. Hike to the top of Moose Mountain (el. 1,148 ft.) and Lookout Mountain (el. 1,200 ft.).

69.name: Charles A. Lindbergh State Park
69.description: Visit this park to hike, picnic and tour the historic home of the Lindberghs—Charles Sr., the U.S. Congressman for whom the park is named, and Charles Jr., the world-famous aviator.

70.name: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park
70.description: You know the lighthouse, but have you seen the waterfalls along Split Rock River, skipped stones at Pebble Beach, or hiked and skied this park’s beautiful trails? Bring bikes and ride the Gitchi-Gami State Trail to Gooseberry Falls State Park.

71.name: Red River State Recreation Area
71.description: This recreation area, new in 2004, replaced property destroyed by the 1997 flood with a 1,200-acre greenway connecting several city parks. The area features a municipal pool, paved trails, river fishing, and a campground with nearby shopping and dining. Campground closed from late October to early May.

72.name: Sibley State Park
72.description: From fishing to swimming to year-round interpretive programs, there’s something for everyone at this popular park in west-central Minnesota. Hike up Mount Tom (el. 1,375 ft.) for a panoramic view or bike the nearby Glacial Lakes State Trail.

73.name: Sakatah Lake State Park
73.description: Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail runs through this park and stretches 39 miles from Mankato to Faribault. The paved trail takes hikers, bikers, skiers, and snowmobilers through scenic woods. Sakatah Lake, a natural widening of the Cannon River, lures canoeists and anglers.

74.name: Rice Lake State Park
74.description: Long ago, American Indians harvested wild rice from this lake, which attracts many waterfowl during migrations. Visitors enjoy photographing spring wildflowers, picnicking, and birdwatching. Camping options include drive-in, walk-in, cart-in, and canoe-in sites.

75.name: Frontenac State Park
75.description: Perched on the Mississippi River, this park is a birdwatcher’s paradise, where more than 260 species have been observed. Visitors also flock here to see wildflowers, fall color, and winter beauty.

77.name: Great River Bluffs State Park
77.description: This park’s diverse landscape—which includes scenic blufftop views of the Mississippi River Valley—is particularly beautiful in the fall. Keep your eyes on the sky; the river valley is a major flyway for waterfowl, eagles, and hawks.

78.name: Itasca State Park
78.description: Stand under towering pines at Preacher’s Grove, explore Wilderness Drive by car or bike, and wade across the Mississippi River as it begins its 2,552-mile journey to the Gulf of Mexico here in Minnesota’s oldest state park.

839.name: Pine Ridge Campground: Oak & Spruce Loops

994.name: Pine Ridge Campground: Pine & Poplar Loops

79.name: Kilen Woods State Park
79.description: Hike along the tranquil Des Moines River or enjoy the view of the river valley from Dinosaur Ridge Overlook. Other popular activities include canoeing, fishing, picnicking, and camping.

81.name: Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area
81.description: Ride 22 miles of single-track mountain bike trails; paddle the scenic shoreline and fish clear lakes full of trout, northern, bass, and panfish; and visit the Croft Mine.

86.name: Franz Jevne State Park
86.description: Scenic trails follow the shoreline of the Rainy River, a fishing haven, and loop back through the woods. Scrambling up the large rock outcrop takes you high above the river.  Wildlife sightings here have included deer, bears, wolves, moose and eagles.

88.name: McCarthy Beach State Park
88.description: Relax at a nationally recognized beach, hike and ski scenic trails within the park, or go snowmobiling, mountain biking, and horseback riding on the Taconite State Trail.

89.name: Glacial Lakes State Park
89.description: Stand on top of the scenic glacial hills and experience the vast, open prairie that once dominated Minnesota. Summer visitors enjoy swimming and fishing in the ultra-clear waters of Mountain Lake.

90.name: Lake Louise State Park
90.description: The Little Iowa and Upper Iowa rivers converge in this park, a peaceful mix of woods and meadows with a beach and access to the 14-mile paved Shooting Star State Trail. Horse and snowmobile trails also wind through the park.

91.name: Lake Shetek State Park
91.description: The word “shetek” is Ojibwe for “pelican,” a bird that visits the park during summer and fall. People visit to fish or swim in southwestern Minnesota’s largest lake, hike the interpretive trail on Loon Island, and bike the scenic, six-mile Casey Jones State Trail.

93.name: Scenic State Park
93.description: A beautiful spot to camp and canoe, this park lives up to its name with sparkling lakes and giant pines. Visitors enjoy fishing, swimming, and hiking in a wilderness-like setting. The Chase Point Trail, atop a mile-long esker, is magnificent.

964.name: Scenic Lake of the Isles Group Camp

94.name: William O Brien State Park
94.description: Discover a beautiful setting for canoeing, fishing, hiking, and other recreation along the banks of the St. Croix River. In winter, 12 miles of groomed trails await classic and skate skiing enthusiasts. Interpretive programs are offered year-round.

95.name: Forestville Mystery Cave State Park
95.description: Journey underground, upstream, and back in time to fully experience everything this blufflands park has to offer. Spring-fed streams provide outstanding trout fishing. Enjoy accessible cave and living history tours. Visit mndnr.gov or call for times and prices.

96.name: Interstate State Park
96.description: The striking rock formations at this park intrigue visitors and attract geologists from all over the world. Hike the bluffs, canoe the St. Croix river, or relax at a riverside picnic. Spring brings a great diversity of wildflowers and in fall, the forest is ablaze with bright colors.

97.name: Monson Lake State Park
97.description: Excellent fishing lures anglers to this park throughout the year. While waiting for a bite, watch the sky and shore for a variety of birds, including herons and white pelicans.

98.name: Moose Lake State Park
98.description: A quiet place to fish and swim, this park also has a must-see Agate and Geological Interpretive Center, open Memorial Weekend through Labor Day. The nearby Willard Munger State Trail is paved from Hinckley to Duluth.

99.name: Old Mill State Park
99.description: The Middle River meanders through this park, where visitors can cross a swinging bridge, see a century-old grist mill, and enjoy an ever-changing parade of wildflowers along wooded trails
